ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=kx+b$ intersects with the x-axis and y-axis at points $A(-3, 0)$ and $B(0, 2)$ respectively. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx+b>0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \text{\textbf{Solution:}} \quad \text{According to the graph, it is known that the function values of y to the right of point A are all greater than 0. Therefore, when } x > -3, \text{ the function values are greater than 0, that is, } kx + b > 0; \]
\[ \text{Thus, the answer is: } \boxed{x > -3}. \]
